page: UpCloud PREMIUM-8xCPU-32GB is a general-purpose virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with 300 GB of local SSD capacity, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and SHA-NI cryptography extensions.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong single-core capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance reaches 3670.47, placing it in the top 10% tier, while single-threaded bzip3 decompression also ranks in the top tier at 17.43 GB/sec. However, multi-core and overall system benchmarks, such as the stress-ng multi-core score of 22341.89 and Geekbench multi-core score of 9098.0, align with the average tier. A notable performance tradeoff is observed in memory subsystem testing, where the PassMark memory score of 1019.02 falls into the bottom 10% tier, indicating potential bottlenecks for memory-intensive operations despite average memory bandwidth results.

Given its balanced 1:4 CPU-to-RAM ratio and bundled 300 GB SSD storage, this server offers a resource-dense profile suitable for general-purpose workloads. It is well-suited for static web serving, which achieved a throughput of 13.06 GB/sec, and database operations, supported by a PassMark database score of 4423.65 and Redis SET performance of 8.37 million operations per second. It is less optimal for large-scale LLM inference, as demonstrated by weak performance on 7B parameter models, or workloads requiring high-performance memory subsystems.
